basis: Immune-mediated necrotizing scleritis directly destroys and thins the sclera; associated systemic autoimmune diseases are separate.
Defined hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; extracolonic cancer risks do not establish additional organ damage.
Defining vertebral and long-bone dysplasia with contractures; frequencies of reported brain, eye and palatal abnormalities are insufficient to establish common involvement.
Neurodevelopmental and progressive motor disorder with intellectual disability, spastic paraplegia and brain atrophy; hypotonia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Usually a localized cutaneous non-Langerhans histiocytic proliferation; systemic and ocular disease are uncommon.
Meningeal-origin tumor situated within the orbit, commonly arising from the optic nerve sheath.
Inherited aneurysmal disease of the abdominal aorta; no additional defining organ involvement.
Parainfluenza type 2 causes respiratory tract infection, particularly upper airway disease and croup.
Defective dentin causes fragile, severely worn teeth and pulp exposure; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Tuberculous infection directly involves the esophagus; pulmonary involvement is not required by this localized concept.
Androgen-dependent follicular miniaturization causes isolated hair loss; it does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Intellectual disability and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; joint dislocations are explicitly defining despite 2/8 reports. Ocular findings individually occur in 2/8.
Skeletal dysplasia, developmental brain disease and acanthosis define SADDAN; hearing loss reported in 1/3. Cardiac findings in 1/3 lack clear direct attribution.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the lung or bronchial epithelium despite an occult primary lesion.
CTSC deficiency impairs innate antimicrobial function; severe destructive periodontitis spans the spectrum, with palmoplantar keratoderma in its major syndromic forms.
Complex brain malformations cause developmental impairment and seizures; cerebral visual impairment in 6/6 is neurologic, without demonstrated eye damage.
Joint hypermobility syndrome is an arthropathy affecting locomotor connective tissues; systemic involvement is not established by this concept.
Trichomonas infection affects vulvovaginal reproductive tissues, which have no anatomical axis; urethral or bladder involvement is not intrinsic.
Benign tumor originates in a cutaneous sebaceous gland.
Lysosomal lipid storage with defining juvenile neurodegeneration; splenic storage affects roughly half or more. Persistent hepatic dysfunction is less consistent in this onset group.
Ventricular cardiac rhythm disorder; syncope or hypoperfusion does not establish common lasting damage to another organ.
Loss of lower-body motor function, typically from spinal cord damage; paralysis does not itself establish primary muscle disease.
Inherited sialic-acid biosynthesis defect impairs platelet production and survival. Myopathy is variable without evidence of ≥30%; bleeding sites do not establish other organ disease.
Acquired ACTH deficiency causes secondary adrenal insufficiency; autoimmunity is annotated at 80–99%. Associated autoimmune diseases and separately diagnosed anemia are excluded.
Bacterial abscess occupies peritonsillar tissues in the pharynx, included in the pulmonary axis.
